overview: Babylon Labour Tracker is a custom web app that ties every hour of shop-floor labour to a manufacturing order and an operation, so a contract manufacturer knows what each batch really costs in labour.

Client: Babylon, a US private-label manufacturer of cosmetics, personal care and pet grooming products (cleansers, serums, moisturisers, shampoos, conditioners, shower gels, body butters, dog shampoo), working under FDA cGMP.
Sites and departments: Manufacturing, Warehouse and "Our Babylon"; all workers on-site; timestamps in Pacific time.
Scale at review: 10 active workers, 125+ manufacturing orders, 342 time entries, 3,958.8 tracked hours, about $84.4k of labour cost.
What it replaces: paper timesheets, a separate HR system and manual SOP sign-off sheets, in one bilingual (English / Spanish) app.
areas: PIN or NFC clock-in, breaks, overtime warnings, admin edits with an audit trail
Assign workers to an MO × operation, start/pause/complete timers, labour cost per task
Employee records, compensation, bonus/commission/equity, EEO, benefits, emergency contacts
PTO and sick accrual, requests, approvals, balance ledger and projections
GMP/SOP training with read-time gating, disciplinary incidents with policy acknowledgement
challenges: Order-level labour costs were missing. Odoo held the orders, but hours were logged for a whole shift. The team could not reliably connect labour cost to a batch or production step.
Attendance relied on manual records. Supervisors handled clock times, breaks and corrections without a clear history of changes.
Training records were hard to review. Paper SOP sign-offs made it difficult to check which workers had completed the required training.
Everyday tools needed two languages. Workers needed screens, SOPs and policies in both English and Spanish.
brief: The team needed a simple shared-device app for workers, with clear records that managers could use for payroll, batch costing and audits.
roles: Manage production, attendance, employee records, planning, leave, reports, training and NFC setup.
Oversee daily production, worker activity and reporting. This portal was outside the source review.
Pick name from a kiosk list, enter a 4-digit PIN, or tap an NFC tag
Clock in and out, manage breaks and tasks, view personal records, complete training and request time off.
roleNotes: Kiosk-first worker flow: the worker list is searchable by name or employee ID, so a shared tablet at the door works without personal logins.
Role checks in code: the front end gates screens on three roles: admin, manager, employee.
Org chart: each worker record shows a manager and a "view in org chart" link.
adminIntro: Twelve admin tools bring production, attendance, people and reporting into one workspace. A shared top bar includes notifications, language and theme controls.

admin.title: Dashboard
paragraphs: See active workers, breaks, today’s recorded hours and total labour cost in one view. Charts break down hours and labour cost by worker.

admin.title: Production Control Matrix
paragraphs: Each row is a manufacturing order; each column is an operation such as weighing, batching or filling.
Review the product, order reference, scheduled date, quantity and status. Open a cell to assign workers or review an active task.
Each assignment shows the worker’s rate, task status and running timer, with controls to start, pause or remove the assignment.

admin.title: Control Table
paragraphs: Review attendance and production-task entries in Pacific time. Search by worker, date and status, or add a missed punch manually.
Attendance records show clock-in, clock-out, duration and change history. Task records also show the order, operation, cost and current status.
Admins can correct shifts and individual breaks with a reason recorded in the audit trail.

admin.title: Manufacturing Orders
paragraphs: Search orders by reference, product, SKU, quantity, purchase order, scheduled date and production status.
Pin or reorder rows to organise the production matrix. Sync the latest orders from Odoo, or create an order manually.

admin.title: Employee Activity
paragraphs: See who is working, on break or off shift for a selected day. Admins can record clock-ins, clock-outs and breaks on a worker’s behalf, with a daily activity log.

admin.title: Workers (people and HR)
paragraphs: Find active or archived workers by name, employee ID, job and work mode. Create a new employee profile or archive an existing one.
Personal and Job tabs hold contact details, reporting lines and dated employment and compensation records. PIN reset and onboarding controls support access setup.
Training, Emergency, Time Off and Benefits tabs keep related records together. Pay changes retain their history for accurate task costing.

admin.title: Operations
paragraphs: Maintain the ten shared production operations. Adding an operation creates a new column in every manufacturing order’s matrix.

admin.title: Future Planning
paragraphs: Assign a worker, order, operation and date before a shift begins. Planned tasks appear in the worker’s assignments and can be cancelled when plans change.

admin.title: Time Off (Leave Management)
paragraphs: Review PTO and sick-time requests by employee, dates and hours. Filter pending or completed decisions, then approve or reject a request.

admin.title: Reports
paragraphs: Filter by worker, order, operation and date. Review recorded hours, labour cost, average hourly cost and training completion.
Charts and entry-level tables provide the detail behind each total. Export the filtered records to CSV.

admin.title: Discipline
paragraphs: Record an incident under SOP 3.7 with its date, category, severity, description and supporting attachments. Keep related policies, action steps and worker acknowledgements together.

admin.title: NFC Setup
paragraphs: Assign a physical NFC tag to a worker and review existing assignments. On supported devices, the worker can then tap the tag to clock in or out.

worker: Clock in, manage breaks and review today’s hours. Start, pause, resume or complete assigned tasks, then check recent activity. NFC works on supported devices; a manual fallback is available.
Their own HR record (identity, address, contacts, social links, education), editable
Their disciplinary incidents, and any policy they must read and sign by typing their full legal name
Read required SOPs in English or Spanish, complete the reading period and record an acknowledgement. Core training and role-specific SOPs are grouped separately.
PTO and sick balances in hours, request form (type, dates, hours, reason), request history and a ledger of hours used, earned and running balance
Light or dark theme, English or Spanish
workerNotes: SOPs open in a timed reader. After the required reading period, the worker can confirm completion. That acknowledgement updates the training record and reporting view.
Clock-out guards work in progress. If tasks are still running, the worker must choose to pause or complete them all before clocking out.
workflows: Corrections: an admin adds a manual entry for a missed punch, or edits breaks with a reason; each change stays in the audit record.

Leave: a worker requests PTO or sick time, an admin approves or rejects it, and the balance ledger updates. Sick time accrues from hours worked up to a 40-hour cap, and admins can project future balances to a chosen date.
Compliance: a worker reads each SOP for the minimum time and confirms it; incidents are logged with a severity, linked to a policy, and acknowledged by the worker with a typed signature.
integration: Odoo stays the system of record for what to make; the app adds the labour layer on top and keeps its own data in Supabase.
technology: Odoo sync: "Sync Orders" calls a server route, /api/sync-odoo, which fetches the latest MOs and updates existing rows ("Fetch latest orders? This will update existing records."). Orders deleted in the app are kept in a deleted_manufacturing_orders table so a sync does not bring them back. Each MO carries number, product, SKU, quantity, PO number, scheduled date, status and an event ID that looks like a calendar event reference.
Front end: React built with Vite, hosted on Vercel; Font Awesome icons; charts for the dashboard and reports; full English/Spanish i18n.

Back end: Supabase (Postgres, auth with password and Google, realtime subscriptions so the matrix, control table and notifications update live). Tables seen in the code: users, activity_logs, tasks, operations, manufacturing_orders, worker_rate_history, leave_requests, leave_history, training_materials, disciplinary_incidents, disciplinary_policies, disciplinary_actions, policy_acknowledgments, attachments.
Events logged: clock_in, clock_out, break_start, break_end, task_start, task_pause, task_resume, task_edit, manual_entry, overtime_warning.
Costing: each task's duration × the worker's hourly rate at that time (rate history is kept), so a raise does not rewrite past costs.
Hardware: Web NFC lets a phone or tablet read a tag to clock a worker in or out; browsers without it get a typed simulator.
finding: Attendance was used daily, but most recent hours were recorded as General Shift. Without an assigned order and operation, batch-level labour costs remained incomplete.
observations: Most recent entries are "Unassigned / General Shift"
